paragraphs: Rabbi Ilai son of Rabbi Elazar ([Shabbat 60a](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.60a.11)); Rabbi Yochanan son of Elazar ([Pesachim 51a](https://www.sefaria.org/Pesachim.51a.12)); Rabbi Yonatan son of Elazar ([Shabbat 49a](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.49a.13-14)); Rabbi Yitzchak son of Elazar ([Shabbat 29b](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.29b.7)); Rabbi Yirmeyah son of Elazar ([Berakhot 58a](https://www.sefaria.org/Berakhot.58a.1)); Rabbi Yishmael ben Elazar ([Shabbat 32a](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.32a.9)); Rabbi Nechemyah ben Elazar (Eichah Rabbah, the section beginning 'and He did not remember His footstool'); Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar, the well-known Tanna.[^2]

notes.text: The heading provides Elazar for the abbreviated patronyms. The list does not establish that all entries share a single father.

The linked texts supply full patronymics for six distinct occurrences. In Pesachim, Rabbah bar bar Chana quotes Yochanan son of Elazar recounting a visit to a garden. The list’s shared patronymic leaves the relationship among the fathers open.
